newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed as dollar strength reigns.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed as dollar strength reigns.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, after key contracts spent the session battered by the powerful dollar.
Dollar/mark surged above resistance at 1.80 to reach 1.8040 before mild profit-taking capped gains late. Dollar/yen soared and approached 116.

Currency futures slid, with yen and sterling leading losses amid cash options-related weakness. Traders cited talk of a prominent hedge fund massively buying deep out-of-the-money yen puts and out-of-the-money sterling puts.
September yen fell to a two-month low.
September marks fell to a new contract low early, but marks and Swiss recovered late amid mild profit-taking by nervous dollar longs.

Many traders had expected more speculation about central bank intervention to kick in above 1.80 in the dollar/mark, traders said. Instead, only mild profit-taking developed and traders said the dollar's stellar uptrend remained intact.

In afternoon trade, Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said the central bank shared the Bonn government's support for a strong mark. He said he believed the mark's correction against other key currencies was over.
Earlier, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said the strength of dollar and sterling against the mark was an overreaction.
But floor traders said the mood remained bullish for the dollar.

"I think it will continue to be until we break through technical levels on the downside," an IMM trading floor manager said. He said dollar/mark support at 1.7750, or roughly $0.5658 mark resistance, was a level to watch.
"Below there and we'll see more dollar selling," the desk manager said.
Mexican peso futures collapsed, closing sharply lower. Traders cited a steep slide in Brazilian equity markets that sparked worries in Mexican financial markets.
Early in the session, the dollar initially dipped, then quickly resumed its uptrend on U.S. retail sales data. June retail sales overall rose 0.5 percent versus a forecast for a 0.2 percent gain.
Sales excluding cars were below forecast at up 0.3 percent.
May's sales were revised to down 0.3 percent overall from the original down 0.1 percent.

At the close, September yen futures were down $0.000114 at $0.008732, marks up $0.0020 at $0.5606, Swiss francs up $0.0018 at $0.6835, sterling fell $0.0098 to $1.6746, Canadian dollars fell $0.0011 to $0.7321, Australian dollars were down $0.0031 at $0.7356 and Mexican pesos fell $0.002100 to $0.121950.
